placement_summary.text: Black is a strong fit when a user wants agency, ambition, and power through clear-eyed cost accounting, resource conversion, and refusal to let inherited taboos choose for them.
placement_summary.short_description: Black placement is source-bounded by agency, ambition, opportunity, self-interest, cost accounting, and resource conversion rather than generic evil or villain-coded aesthetics.
placement_summary.best_fit_summary: wants self-directed agency, power, opportunity, and practical leverage while accepting costs and tradeoffs that serve a concrete goal
placement_summary.poor_fit_summary: wants darkness, cruelty, villainy, mechanics, Commander card names, or reckless danger without Black's source-backed power, self-advocacy, opportunity, or cost-conversion logic
placement_summary.interpretation_warning: Placement data is Vox Mana interpretation and should be treated as a matching heuristic, not direct Wizards canon or moral judgment.

moral_and_psychological_profile.primary_drive: Secure the power to choose one's own life by using opportunities and resources others may refuse.
moral_and_psychological_profile.ethical_pressure: A tool that wins can still leave a debt; self-advocacy can become isolation or exploitation.
moral_and_psychological_profile.core_boundary: Placement language is Vox Mana interpretation from source-backed color philosophy, not official personality canon or moral judgment.

placement_axes.label: Power as Agency
placement_axes.description: Measures how much the user centers power as the condition for freedom and self-determination.
placement_axes.rationale: Black's goal is power and opportunity as a route to control over life.

placement_axes.label: Cost Conversion
placement_axes.description: Separates Black's willingness to pay costs from reckless harm or generic ambition.
placement_axes.rationale: Black accepts costs, sacrifice, and risk when they produce success.

placement_axes.label: Self-Interest Shadow
placement_axes.description: Tracks whether the user wants self-advocacy or total disregard for consequences.
placement_axes.rationale: Black's strength and weakness both come from willingness to use dangerous tools.

behavioral_signals: the user names power or agency as the real need
the user accepts tradeoffs and costs when they buy freedom
the user distrusts moral stories that ask them to act against self-interest
the user sees fear, death, or loss as resources to understand rather than deny
the user prefers calculated risk over waiting for permission
inhibitor_traits: group morality as the final authority
natural destiny or role acceptance over self-authorship
power pursued so blindly it stops serving the self
inhibitor_traps: The answer moralizes Black as evil rather than analyzing power.
The answer wants ambition but refuses to pay any meaningful cost.
The answer is reckless impulse rather than calculated ruthlessness.
The answer turns every relationship into leverage without any practical boundary.
good_fit_indicators: power as the route to self-determination
calculated ruthlessness rather than mere cruelty
resource conversion, sacrifice, or graveyard value
ideal_fit_indicators: the user can name what they want and what they will spend to get it
the user sees fear or loss as information, not a stop sign
the user values being their own advocate
the user wants leverage that changes material conditions
poor_fit_indicators: group good over self-interest in every conflict
improvement for its own sake without concrete power
risk-taking that ignores whether it actually serves the goal

discriminator_questions.question: Is the user seeking power as agency, or merely trying to be edgy or cruel?
discriminator_questions.purpose: Separates Black's source-backed self-advocacy from stereotype.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_supports_this_factio: Supports Black when power is tied to opportunity, survival, control over life, or material leverage.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_weakens_this_faction: Weakens Black when cruelty is aimless or when power is only aesthetic.

discriminator_questions.question: Does the user accept costs because they serve the goal, or are they just courting danger?
discriminator_questions.purpose: Separates calculated Black risk from Red recklessness.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_supports_this_factio: Supports Black when the user weighs sacrifice, cost, and opportunity methodically.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_weakens_this_faction: Weakens Black when risk is impulsive, performative, or disconnected from gain.

discriminator_questions.question: Is self-interest being treated as honest advocacy, or as denial of all responsibility?
discriminator_questions.purpose: Catches Black's self-consuming shadow and Green/White collisions.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_supports_this_factio: Supports Black when self-interest is clear, strategic, and connected to agency.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_weakens_this_faction: Weakens Black when the answer collapses into nihilism or refuses any consequence accounting.

discriminator_questions.question: Are removal, discard, sacrifice, reanimation, life payment, drain, or creature-type cues being used as Black texture rather than Black identity proof?
discriminator_questions.purpose: Keeps mechanical examples source-bound and prevents mechanics or Commander rows from becoming Black philosophy.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_supports_this_factio: Supports Black only when mechanics are treated as dated color-pie texture tied to cost, resource conversion, life, death, or leverage.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_weakens_this_faction: Weakens Black when card names, Commander support rows, or mechanics are treated as philosophy or placement-axis evidence.

collision_guidance.rule: Black is power through self-advocacy and cost conversion, not objective evil, aimless cruelty, or reckless danger.
review_triggers: rules language used as exact legality without CR verification

pairs.separator: Black asks what secures the self; White asks what the group needs.
pairs.ask: Is the user willing to subordinate self-interest to shared obligation?

pairs.separator: Black asserts self-directed will; Green trusts role, interdependence, and natural order.
pairs.ask: Does the user want to seize opportunity or fulfill a place in the web?

calibration_tuning.false_positive_guardrail: Do not place Black for darkness, villainy, or cruelty alone; require power, agency, self-interest, opportunity, or cost conversion.

use_when: Use Black when the user centers power, agency, ambition, cost, or resource conversion.
Frame Black as clear-eyed self-advocacy rather than objective evil.
Keep commander candidates deferred unless current legality verification is done.
avoid_when: The user wants group-first morality as the binding answer.
The user wants natural role acceptance over self-authorship.
The answer only contains darkness or villainy without power logic.
how_to_recognize_mismatch: group good over self-interest in every conflict
improvement for its own sake without concrete power
card names, creature types, or mechanics treated as Black philosophy proof
chatbot_guidance.calibration_note: Black should rise only when ambition, self-advocacy, cost, and power are materially important.
never_claim_as_canon: Vox Mana placement axes are official Wizards color-pie scores.
A candidate mono-black commander is Layer 2 support without current verification.
